narrative.summary: At the Cliffside Hotel’s fencing academy, Katherine Quayle is found stabbed dead in her room, which was locked and sealed from all visible entry points. The foggy seaside setting and strict hotel layout suggest an impossible murder. Suspicion falls on Hector Gaunt, Katherine’s rival and fellow fencing master, but his alibi and the apparent locked room puzzle investigators. The detective uncovers a hidden coastal tidal cave path that the killer exploited at low tide to enter and exit undetected, revealing the truth behind the spatial impossibility.

accepted_facts: Katherine Quayle was stabbed with a fencing foil to the heart in her locked room.
The victim’s door and windows were locked and sealed from inside.
A tide chart pinned in the hotel lobby shows an unusually low tide at the time of murder.
Scratches and fresh seaweed were found on the cliffside rocks beneath the victim’s east window.
Saltwater corrosion marks were found on the iron latch of the lower east window.
Hector Gaunt’s alibi places him in the billiard room from eight o’clock to half past eight.
The victim’s estimated time of death was between eight twenty and eight forty-five.
inferred_conclusions: The murder occurred during the low tide window when the tidal cave was accessible.
Hector Gaunt could have used the tidal cave to enter the victim’s room through the lower east window.
The locked doors and windows did not prevent ingress or egress via the tidal cave path.
The saltwater corrosion on the window latch indicates it was not secured tightly.
The scratches and seaweed trace Hector Gaunt’s path on the cliffside rocks.

mechanism.description: The killer exploited a natural tidal cave beneath the hotel’s eastern cliffside, accessible only at unusually low tide. The victim’s lower east window, normally assumed sealed, had a loosely secured iron latch corroded by saltwater, allowing entry from the tidal cave. The door and upper windows were locked internally, creating a false assumption of no access. The tidal cave’s accessibility was hidden by the fog and the timing of the tide, which was unusually low at the murder time, allowing the killer to enter and leave without being seen.

delivery_path.step: The tide chart shows a rare low tide exposing the tidal cave entrance beneath the hotel.
Fresh scratches and seaweed on cliffside rocks beneath the victim’s lower east window indicate recent passage.
Saltwater corrosion on the iron latch of the lower east window shows it was not tightly secured.
The killer used the tidal cave to access the victim’s room through the lower east window, bypassing locked doors.

outcome.result: The killer, Hector Gaunt, was able to enter and exit the victim’s locked room by exploiting the tidal cave and corroded latch, invalidating his alibi and revealing the spatial impossibility of the murder.

false_assumption.statement: The victim’s room was completely sealed and inaccessible from outside because all doors and windows were locked from the inside.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: All visible access points were locked and sealed; the hotel layout and fog prevented outside movement; standard hotel protocols ensured room security.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: A hidden natural tidal cave beneath the hotel allowed access to the victim’s room through a loosely secured lower east window, bypassing all locked doors and upper windows.

supporting_points: Neville had a known grudge against Hector and was seen near the hotel corridors around the murder time.
Neville’s alibi was weaker and placed him near the victim’s floor, making him a plausible suspect.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Neville’s fingerprints and glove marks were not found on the murder weapon or around the victim’s room, and he could not have accessed the victim’s room due to locked doors and windows.

red_herrings.description: Glove marks matching Neville Lachlan’s gloves were found on the fencing foil in the victim’s room.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Neville had handled the fencing foil during a training session the day before the murder, leaving glove marks unrelated to the crime.

red_herrings.description: A torn letter threatening the victim was found in Bertram Vance’s room.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The letter was a forged prank by a junior staff member unrelated to the murder.

closed_circle.rationale: All persons present in the hotel and with plausible access to the victim and murder weapon at the relevant time form the closed suspect pool. No outsiders had access to the hotel or the victim’s room during the murder.

discriminating_test.design: The discriminating test compares tidal, murder, and saltwater against the claimed timeline.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The tidal cave path was accessible only during the victim’s time of death, and Hector Gaunt uniquely had the opportunity and means to use it to commit the murder.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The reenactment confirms the tidal cave opens exactly during the murder window and that entry through the lower east window is possible and practical, proving Hector Gaunt’s presence at the scene.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1: Saltwater corrosion on the lower east window latch (early) reveals a potential access point. Step 2: Scratches and seaweed traces on cliffside rocks (mid) show recent passage through the tidal cave. Step 3: Traces of the fencing foil on the cliffside path linked to Hector Gaunt (mid) connect the murder weapon to the suspect. Step 4: Hector Gaunt’s alibi gap (mid) invalidates his claimed presence elsewhere. All clues are presented before the discriminating test, allowing the reader to deduce the culprit logically.
